output.question: What lawsuits involve Celsius?
output.answer: I took 'Celsius' to mean Celsius Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: CELH), the energy-drink maker. The newest case is a federal securities class action in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida (No. 26-cv-62465). It covers investors who bought shares between February 21, 2025 and June 3, 2026, and claims Celsius did not disclose the cardiac risks of its Alani Nu drinks or that it was marketing them to minors. The lead-plaintiff deadline was November 3, 2026. The complaint points to two events that sent the stock down. On April 9, 2026, a wrongful-death lawsuit was reported over a 17-year-old's death linked to Alani Nu. On June 4, 2026, the Texas Attorney General announced an investigation. Celsius's Q2 2026 10-Q also lists a consolidated securities class action, several shareholder derivative suits (Flannery, Sunny, Murphy, Dobler and Stoyanoff), and the Strong Arm Productions (rapper Flo Rida) contract case. In that case the Florida Supreme Court declined review in November 2025, and on April 17, 2026 the trial court entered a new judgment of about $101.1 million including prejudgment interest. It is not public whether Celsius has paid it or is still challenging it.

key_facts.fact: A securities class action against Celsius Holdings and certain officers is pending in S.D. Florida, docket 26-cv-62465. It claims violations of Exchange Act Sections 10(b) and 20(a) and Rule 10b-5 and covers February 21, 2025 to June 3, 2026. The lead-plaintiff deadline was November 3, 2026.

The complaint claims Celsius failed to disclose the cardiac risks of Alani Nu drinks (200 mg of caffeine per 12 oz) and marketed them to minors through college ambassadors. Celsius bought Alani Nu on April 1, 2025 for a net $1.65 billion.

On April 9, 2026, a wrongful-death lawsuit was reported over a 17-year-old's death allegedly linked to Alani Nu, and the stock fell $1.52 (4.18%) to $34.86 on April 10. On June 4, 2026, the Texas Attorney General announced an investigation, and the stock fell $2.26 (7.53%) to $27.75.

Celsius's Q2 2026 10-Q lists a consolidated Securities Class Action (two putative securities class actions combined) and shareholder derivative actions brought by Suzanne Flannery, Shadia Khan Sunny, David Murphy, Kurt Dobler and Mark Stoyanoff. It also lists the Strong Arm Productions lawsuit.

In the Strong Arm Productions (Flo Rida) case, the Florida Supreme Court declined review in November 2025. On April 17, 2026 the trial court entered a new judgment of about $101.1 million including prejudgment interest. It is not publicly confirmed whether Celsius has paid it.

caveats: 'Celsius' could also mean Celsius Network, the bankrupt crypto lender. Its litigation is separate: the bankruptcy litigation administrator's claims against former CEO Alex Mashinsky and others, the FTC case, and New York AG actions. This answer does not cover it.

The class-action details come from a plaintiff-firm press release, so they are allegations and not proven. The 10-Q's full legal-proceedings note (amounts, accruals, case status) was cut off in what I could read, so the figures and status of the derivative suits and the Strong Arm accrual come from secondary sources or are not verified.

The $101.1M Strong Arm judgment comes from a secondary legal site (LawFold) whose own body text contradicts its update box. Check the Broward County docket or Celsius's 10-Q/10-K before relying on it.

A second Strong Arm suit filed December 26, 2025 seeks ongoing Sparkling Orange royalties (motion to dismiss argued July 15, 2026). A search summary mentioned it, but I could not confirm it on a page I opened.
The wrongful-death suit and the Texas AG investigation are described only as cited in the class-action release. Neither filing was opened. The Texas matter is an investigation, not a lawsuit.
